A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCALE optimizer study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCALE pretraining results, normalization and momentum experiments, timing measurements, and gradient-variance analyses. Some comparator scores are explicitly attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds training-throughput measurements, additional model configurations, overtraining experiments, GLUE fine-tuning, and mixed-normalization ablations.

M1.justification: SCALE retains column-wise normalization and first-order momentum restricted to the output layer. Adam updates for vector parameters and Muon-style scaling for the 1B model were already documented in v1. Algorithm 1 now consistently uses the already-defined mini-batch gradient, repairing notation without establishing a different optimization procedure.

E1.justification: v1's task evaluation concerns C4 language-model pretraining. v2 adds RoBERTa-base fine-tuning on six GLUE tasks: RTE, CoLA, MRPC, STS-B, SST-2, and QNLI (Appendix A.6, Table 11). This substantially expands data and task coverage. The additional decoder architectures still use C4 and constitute configuration changes.

E2.justification: The main comparator roster largely persists, but Table 6 adds Muon to the previously APOLLO/APOLLO-Mini-only 7B comparison. Table 2 drops Muon, while Table 3 replaces its Muon reference row with Adam and Adam (Stable-SPAM). Stable-SPAM's renaming does not introduce another method. The original 1B SWAN comparison survives in v2's Table 5 caption.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes the 1B training budget from 13.1B to 20B tokens. v2 also introduces Qwen2-500M, GPT2-M, and Gemma-2B configurations, 350M training at 15.6B and 31.2B tokens, a tokens-per-second evaluation on four H100 GPUs, and fine-tuning with learning-rate search and best-epoch selection. Existing LLaMA sequence length, batch size, precision, and scheduling settings are retained and relocated to Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: v2 adds mixed-normalization ablations holding last-layer momentum fixed (Table 12), LM-head gradient histograms and token-column diagnostics (Figures 3 and 7), training-budget sensitivity (Table 10), and training-throughput analysis (Table 7). The original learning-rate sensitivity and layer-variance analyses remain. The small comparison without Muon-style learning-rate scaling reported in v1 Appendix A.2 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or documented seed replication. The single-run disclosure for 7B SCALE is retained and extended to the added Muon result using the same reporting practice. Gradient-distribution diagnostics do not add uncertainty estimates for experimental performance.

E6.justification: The 1B results are replaced under a longer budget: SCALE reports 14.25 perplexity at 13.1B tokens in v1 and 13.49 at 20B in v2, rather than a same-setting improvement. Table 6 retains SCALE's 12.59 and adds Muon's 12.72. Tables 7–12 add substantial results, including SCALE throughput of 44,728 tokens/second and GLUE averages of 85.51 for SCALE versus 85.68 for Adam.

T1.justification: The convergence assumptions, bound, and appendix proof are retained; the new main-text proof sketch restates existing arguments. However, v2 defines the gradient in Eq. (2.8) as a stochastic sample gradient, whereas both appendix proofs define it as the full-loss gradient before Eq. (A.10). This changes the stated stationarity quantity and introduces an internal mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The central two-component optimizer and 35–45% memory claim persist. v2 reframes the research question from minimal optimizer states to minimal modifications to SGD and extends the abstract's 7B superiority claim from APOLLO to APOLLO and Muon. The contribution as a minimalist baseline remains in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 attributes poor row-wise normalization to extreme LM-head gradient values and hypothesizes that column normalization balances learning across frequent and rare tokens (Section 2.1, Appendix A.9). It adds an interpretation of architectural generality and explicitly qualifies fine-tuning applicability: pretraining remains the target, replacing PEFT is not expected, and combining SCALE with PEFT is future work. These explanations and boundaries were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the four-H100 throughput setup and the Newton-Schulz surrogate used for unavailable SWAN throughput measurements. It also supplies diagnostic iteration and tokenizer details and fine-tuning selection procedures. Existing SCALE learning rates, momentum coefficient, vector-parameter handling, and code link remain unchanged; much of Appendix A.2 simply consolidates previously disclosed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds SM3, CAME, a SWAN variant, and a connection to Kunstner et al. (2024) on class imbalance, alongside references supporting the new architectures and tasks. Sophia and standalone SPAM discussion and references are removed, while Stable-SPAM remains. The central positioning as a minimalist memory-efficient optimizer is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten, related work is reorganized, and the normalization exposition is recast from an explicit steepest-descent formulation into a direct list of normalization schemes. A main-text proof sketch is added, experimental settings move into Appendix A.2, and existing appendix analyses are reordered. These changes substantially revise the exposition while retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds diagnostic Figures 3 and 7 and Tables 7–12. The original 1B training-curve Figure 4 becomes Figure 6 with a longer iteration axis and additional comparator curves. Table 4 is restructured, and several main-text tables are resized and placed beside prose. The original variance and learning-rate plots are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily supported SCALE through LLaMA/C4 experiments and isolated normalization timings. v2 substantially strengthens practical-efficiency, generality, and design-justification evidence through training throughput, additional architectures, longer training budgets, GLUE evaluations, mixed-normalization ablations, and the 7B Muon comparison. These gains outweigh the localized theorem-definition inconsistency. Run-level uncertainty remains absent, so small performance margins still provide limited support for broad superiority claims.
